questions.q: What is restaurant reputation management software?
questions.a: It's a tool that pulls your reviews and guest feedback from sites like Google, Yelp, Tripadvisor and delivery apps into one place so your team can track and reply to them. Most platforms also analyze sentiment and show trends by location. That makes it much easier to spot recurring problems once you run more than a handful of restaurants.

questions.q: How much does restaurant reputation management software cost?
questions.a: Prices range from free tools to several hundred dollars per month, depending on how many locations you have, your review volume and the features you need. Basic monitoring and alerts sit at the low end, while multi-location analytics and automation cost more. Many vendors only quote on request, so ask what extra locations, integrations and onboarding will add to the total.

questions.q: Does replying to reviews really help a restaurant's revenue?
questions.a: Yes, consistent replies tend to lift your average rating, and a better rating makes guests more likely to choose you. The post cites Michael Luca's Harvard study, which linked a one-star increase to higher revenue. Replying to more reviews is one of the most direct ways to start that loop.

questions.q: How do I choose the right reputation management tool for my restaurant?
questions.a: Start with where your guests leave feedback and make sure the tool covers those sites. Then check sentiment analysis, multi-location dashboards, alerts, reporting and integrations with your POS, reservation system and CRM. Ease of use matters too, since managers need to see quickly what needs attention.

questions.q: Can AI write replies to restaurant reviews?
questions.a: Yes, many platforms now draft or send AI-written replies so no review goes unanswered. With Momos, every review lands in a Unified Inbox and AI replies in your brand's tone, which you can shape with a brand guideline or a response library. You'll still want to review how negative feedback gets routed to the right team.

questions.q: What should I track after rolling out reputation management software?
questions.a: Watch review volume, average rating on each key platform, response rate and response time. Sentiment trends and the share of negative reviews show whether guest experience is actually improving. Comparing these by location helps you find the restaurants that need support first.
